title: Steady heat flow through a layered wall
prompt: Implement solve(payload) for one-dimensional steady conduction through layers in series. Each layer supplies thickness_m (nonnegative), conductivity_w_mk (positive), and area_m2 (positive). Boundary temperatures are hot_c and cold_c; the names do not require hot_c>=cold_c. Resistance is thickness/(conductivity*area) in K/W. Return {"heat_flow_w":Q,"interface_temperatures_c":[T0,...,Tn]} where Q=(hot_c-cold_c)/sum(R), T0=hot_c and Ti+1=Ti-Q*Ri. Include both boundaries, and preserve repeated temperatures across zero-thickness layers. Return {"error":"invalid_layers"} for no layers, an invalid layer dimension, or nonpositive total resistance. All supplied numbers are finite with representable arithmetic. Do not mutate input. Absolute/relative tolerance 1e-8.
bad_solution:
def solve(payload):
    layers = payload["layers"]
    total = sum(layer["thickness_m"] / layer["conductivity_w_mk"] for layer in layers)
    heat = (payload["hot_c"] - payload["cold_c"]) / total
    n = len(layers)
    temperatures = [payload["hot_c"] + (payload["cold_c"] - payload["hot_c"]) * i / n for i in range(n + 1)]
    return {"heat_flow_w": heat, "interface_temperatures_c": temperatures}
